proof_review.notes: The chapter states no theorem and contains no deductive proof.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external scheduler benchmark, conformance test, failure injection, autoscaler experiment, capacity study, or production rollout is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently separates declared demand, hard feasibility, weighted preference, trusted node state, topology, storage/device reachability, priority/preemption, binding, kubelet admission, readiness, and continuing placement drift.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can derive requests, compose selectors/affinity/taints/spread, coordinate storage/devices/autoscaling, govern priority/gates, design dedicated pools, observe every placement stage, and diagnose Pending pods without weakening requirements blindly.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence progresses from intent and scheduler cycles through requests, node facts, direct-assignment caveats, taints, affinity, spread, conjunctive feasibility, storage/devices, priority, gates, autoscaling, drift, isolation, observation, diagnosis, and platform products. Ten examples remain distinct; five exercises progress from contract design through unsafe-policy audit, exact skew reasoning, diagnosis, and emergency-team transfer, with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
